articles.headline: Legislation to strengthen penalties against students who attack Louisiana public school employees awaits Governor Jeff Landry’s signature
articles.excerpt: Louisiana lawmakers sent the “Teacher’s Shield Act” to Gov. Jeff Landry’s desk. House Bill 283 mandates automatic expulsion of at least two semesters for students who assault school employees and lets injured teachers use up to a year of sick leave to recover.

articles.headline: Student Armed With Knife Charged After Threatening to Stab Teacher at Great Mills High School
articles.image_alt: Knife seized at Great Mills High School
articles.excerpt: A school resource officer at Great Mills High School was alerted that a student had threatened to stab a teacher. Deputies recovered a weapon and charged the student with possession of a dangerous weapon on school property and disrupting school operations.

articles.headline: Police arrest Monona Grove High School student accused of bringing gun to school
articles.excerpt: Monona police arrested a Monona Grove High School student Thursday after a tip that he brought a gun to campus. Officers recovered the firearm and the teen was booked on charges of possessing a dangerous weapon at school. No threats were made and no one was injured.

articles.headline: Parent accused of assaulting principal, grabbing students at Rowan County school
articles.excerpt: China Grove Elementary went into a one-hour lockdown after a 39-year-old parent refused to leave, grabbed two children by the arms, then assaulted the teacher and principal who intervened. He fought arriving officers and faces six charges including assault on school employees.

articles.headline: Student tackled after pulling loaded gun during hallway fight at Overland High School
articles.image_alt: Overland High School in Aurora, Colorado
articles.excerpt: A 16-year-old pulled a loaded handgun during a hallway fight at Overland High School in Aurora and was tackled and disarmed before anyone was hurt. He faces juvenile charges of weapon possession on school grounds and unlawful possession of a handgun.

articles.headline: St. Landry Parish Student Charged with Battery of a Teacher and Terrorizing
articles.image_alt: St. Landry Parish Sheriff's Office booking photo
articles.excerpt: A 17-year-old was arrested after a seven-student brawl at Northwest High School in which a teacher was hit. Deputies say they recovered audio of the teen threatening to shoot students, and he was booked on battery of a teacher and terrorizing charges.

articles.headline: Bond granted for student arrested after loaded gun found on Richland County school bus
articles.excerpt: An 18-year-old was charged after another student texted 911 to report he had a gun on a bus bound for Blythewood High School. Deputies found a loaded firearm and removed him; a judge later granted bond. The student tip is credited with preventing harm.

articles.headline: Wilson County School Board unanimously approves purchasing four new mobile weapons detection systems
articles.image_alt: Mobile weapons detection scanner at a school
articles.excerpt: The Wilson County School Board voted unanimously to buy four mobile Evolv weapons-detection units for about $440,000, with state grants covering most of the cost. The portable scanners can rotate between schools and events, bringing the district total to 11 systems.

articles.headline: Student violence causes SC teachers to quit. Legislators are working on a solution.
articles.image_alt: South Carolina House education committee hearing
articles.excerpt: South Carolina's Educator Safety and Classroom Authority Act would let teachers use reasonable force in self-defense and permanently remove violent students. A teachers' group reported educators suffering concussions, torn tendons and worse from student assaults.

articles.headline: Reports of student violence against Comal ISD educators surged over 3 school years, data shows
articles.excerpt: A KSAT Investigates review of district records found reports of student violence against Comal ISD educators rose sharply across three school years. Teachers described being hit, bitten and threatened, raising questions about how the Texas district tracks incidents.

archive.headline: Judge dismisses case against former Richneck Elementary assistant principal accused of failing to prevent shooting
archive.image_alt: Richneck Elementary School in Newport News
archive.excerpt: A Virginia judge dismissed all eight felony child-neglect counts against former Richneck assistant principal Ebony Parker mid-trial, ruling that ignoring multiple warnings that a 6-year-old had a gun in his backpack before he shot teacher Abby Zwerner 'is not a crime' under current law.

archive.headline: Antioch High School shooting survivor sues weapons detection company over system's failure to detect shooter's gun
archive.image_alt: Antioch High School building exterior
archive.excerpt: A survivor of the deadly Antioch High School shooting has filed suit against Evolv Technology, alleging the AI scanner failed to detect the gunman's firearm despite being marketed as capable of doing so. The case adds to mounting accountability pressure on weapons-detection vendors.

archive.headline: Charles County Commissioners authorize $430K request to expand weapons detection in public schools
archive.image_alt: Charles County Public Schools security briefing
archive.excerpt: Charles County commissioners voted to submit a $430,000 nonrecurring cost exclusion request to the Maryland State Department of Education to expand weapons-detection coverage across district campuses. The expansion follows two ghost-gun arrests at St. Charles High earlier this month.

archive.headline: Governor DeSantis signs House Bill 757 expanding school safety measures to colleges and universities
archive.excerpt: Florida HB 757, signed by Governor DeSantis at the Commissioner's Summit, makes firing a weapon within 1,000 feet of a school a second-degree felony and requires public colleges to adopt active-assailant response plans. It extends K-12 safety provisions into higher education.

archive.headline: Seminole High School student arrested for bringing gun onto campus, police say
archive.image_alt: Seminole High School Sanford Florida
archive.excerpt: A student tip prompted lockdowns at Seminole High School's main campus and 9th-grade center after a 17-year-old was reported to be carrying a gun. Officers found him hiding in a closet and arrested him on firearm-possession and school-disruption charges.

archive.headline: Weapons detection systems installed at all Metro Nashville Public high schools and middle schools
archive.image_alt: Evolv weapons detection scanner at a school entry
archive.excerpt: Metro Nashville Public Schools has now installed Evolv weapons detection systems at every middle and high school in the district. The rollout began after the deadly Antioch High School shooting in 2025 and represents the largest district-wide deployment in Tennessee.

archive.headline: Three Rutherford County students charged, expelled after officer and teacher assaulted during fight
archive.image_alt: Siegel High School in Rutherford County
archive.excerpt: Three Siegel High School students were charged and expelled after a teacher was repeatedly shoved and an SRO was punched in the face during separate cafeteria altercations. Charges include felony assault on a first responder, resisting arrest, and disorderly conduct.

archive.headline: Laredo teen arrested for social media threat against school
archive.image_alt: Laredo police investigate school threat
archive.excerpt: A 15-year-old boy was arrested Saturday night after Laredo police say he posted threats against a local UISD campus on social media. The Texas Anti-Gang unit and special operations group worked with school police to track him down; he was charged with terroristic threat.

archive.headline: Suspect arraigned in deadly Grand Rapids double shooting; new details revealed in court documents
archive.image_alt: Suspect arraigned in court
archive.excerpt: An 18-year-old was arraigned and denied bond on two counts of open murder after a fatal shooting on the grounds of Southwest Elementary School. Court documents say the suspect drew a handgun during a playground confrontation and opened fire.

archive.headline: Bomb threats against Northeast Ohio school districts continue for 2nd day
archive.image_alt: Northeast Ohio schools with bomb threats
archive.excerpt: For a second consecutive day, Northeast Ohio school districts received bomb threats, prompting evacuations at Elyria High School and Ely Elementary on Friday. Five other districts were swatted on Thursday, all of which authorities believe were hoax calls.

archive.headline: Augusta Prep student arrested over picture of LEGO gun, threat he called a joke
archive.image_alt: Augusta Prep school sign at entrance
archive.excerpt: A senior at Augusta Preparatory Day School was arrested on a terroristic threats charge after posting a Snapchat photo of a pistol with the caption 'shooting up the school so I don't have to take the stats exam.' Deputies determined the 'pistol' was a LEGO build, but a judge issued a warrant.

archive.headline: Buchholz High School locked down due to bomb threat, deputies say
archive.image_alt: Buchholz High School locked down
archive.excerpt: Alachua County Sheriff's deputies locked down Buchholz High School in Gainesville on Friday after an anonymous caller claimed a bomb had been placed inside one of the buildings. Students and staff were secured while a methodical search was conducted.

archive.headline: New bill aims to increase internet safety rules for Tennessee students
archive.image_alt: Student using laptop in classroom
archive.excerpt: A Tennessee bill awaiting the governor's signature would force districts to set strict internet safety rules, block sites with violence or self-harm, and immediately alert parents when a student under 18 breaks the rules. Pre-K through fifth graders would only get hidden, locked-down email accounts.

archive.headline: Senator Darby Hills testifies on commonsense school safety legislation
archive.image_alt: Senator Darby Hills testifying in committee
archive.excerpt: Illinois Senate Bill 2788 would create a voluntary School Resource Officer Grant Program to help districts and police agencies share the cost of putting an SRO in schools that want one. Sen. Darby Hills told the Appropriations Education Committee SROs are out of reach for districts that can't afford them.

archive.headline: Washoe County Sheriff's Office explains role in handling North Valleys High's lockdown incident
archive.image_alt: North Valleys High School lockdown response
archive.excerpt: Washoe County deputies and a K-9 team supported Washoe County School Police during a Thursday lockdown at North Valleys High School in Reno after a report of multiple subjects with a weapon. Four juveniles were involved and an arrest was made.

archive.headline: Student tip leads to arrest of Tenino high schooler who allegedly threatened to bring gun to class
archive.image_alt: Tenino High School exterior
archive.excerpt: A classmate's overnight tip allowed Thurston County deputies to identify and arrest a Tenino High School student before classes started Thursday. The student had allegedly threatened to bring a firearm to school the next day, and was booked for threats to injure school property.

archive.headline: Owen County Sheriff's Office: Gun, drugs found in Owen Valley student's car
archive.image_alt: Police arrest at scene
archive.excerpt: A 16-year-old Owen Valley High School student was taken into custody after allegedly threatening a classmate. A search of his car on school property turned up a gun, drugs, and drug paraphernalia, the Owen County Sheriff's Office said.

archive.headline: Weapons, ammunition found in student's vehicle at Stanley-Boyd school
archive.image_alt: Stanley-Boyd school weapons found
archive.excerpt: Stanley police searched a student's vehicle in the Stanley-Boyd school parking lot Thursday after another student reported a possible weapon. Officers found multiple weapons and rounds of ammunition. The juvenile is being referred to the Chippewa County juvenile court.

archive.headline: Bedford County school placed on lockdown after weapon found in vehicle
archive.image_alt: Shelbyville Central High School entrance
archive.excerpt: Shelbyville Central High School in Bedford County went into lockdown at 10:40 a.m. Wednesday after a weapon was found in a student's vehicle. The student was taken into custody and the weapon confiscated; the district says zero-tolerance discipline still applies even though no harm appeared intended.

archive.headline: Huntsville school leaders address safety concerns after several guns found on campuses throughout Madison Co.
archive.image_alt: Huntsville City Schools press conference
archive.excerpt: Huntsville City Schools leaders held a public safety briefing May 6 after five firearms turned up on Madison County campuses in less than two months. The district is fast-tracking weapon-detection rollout and reinforcing zero-tolerance discipline for students who bring guns to class.

archive.headline: Multiple Kansas schools targeted by statewide swatting incident, police say
archive.image_alt: Kansas police vehicles outside a school
archive.excerpt: Schools in Parsons, Chanute, Humboldt, Fort Scott, Russell and Woodson districts were forced into lockdown May 6 by AI-generated swatting calls. KBI investigators say the calls trace to a foreign criminal enterprise targeting U.S. schools to terrorize students and staff.

archive.headline: Pima County parents concerned about lack of communication after student arrested over threats
archive.image_alt: Walden Grove High School bus pickup area
archive.excerpt: Walden Grove High parents say a student arrested for threatening to bring a gun and bomb to school was back on the bus days later. The Sahuarita Police Department and Sahuarita Unified School District never told families that the threat had been deemed not credible, leaving parents to call 911 themselves.

archive.headline: Pima County student allegedly threatened to bring gun, bomb to school
archive.image_alt: Walden Grove High School in Sahuarita, Arizona
archive.excerpt: A Walden Grove High School student in Sahuarita, Arizona was arrested Saturday after allegedly threatening to bring a gun and bomb to school Monday to hurt others. Pima County deputies booked the juvenile on threats and intimidation charges.

archive.headline: North Haven middle school, high school placed on lockdown as police investigate threat
archive.image_alt: North Haven High School in Connecticut
archive.excerpt: North Haven High School and Middle School were placed on lockdown Tuesday afternoon after police received a threat of violence directed at the high school. North Haven officers are investigating; no actual violence has occurred and students were held in classrooms while law enforcement secured the campus.

archive.headline: PSEA president urges Pa. House committee to pass legislation strengthening protections for educators injured as a result of student behavior
archive.image_alt: Pennsylvania State Capitol in Harrisburg
archive.excerpt: PSEA president Aaron Chapin testified before the Pa. House Education Committee on May 5 in support of legislation expanding paid recovery leave, workers' compensation, and removal authority for teachers injured by student violence. Educator assault reports have climbed sharply in the state.
